requirement.text: If the current temperature value is strictly less than the lower value of the valid temperature range or if the received temperature value is strictly greater than the upper value of the valid temperature range, then the THEMAS system shall identify the current temperature value as an invalid temperature and shall output an invalid temperature status.

classification.rationale: The requirement describes deterministic range checking for temperature readings within a control or monitoring system (THEMAS). It does not involve web interfaces, mobile application components, or machine learning models.

rounds.text_checked: If the current temperature value is strictly less than the lower value of the valid temperature range or if the received temperature value is strictly greater than the upper value of the valid temperature range, then the THEMAS system shall identify the current temperature value as an invalid temperature and shall output an invalid temperature status.

issues.span: shall identify the current temperature value as an invalid temperature and shall output an invalid temperature status
issues.explanation: The requirement bundles two separate testable behaviors (identifying the temperature as invalid and outputting an invalid temperature status) into a single requirement statement.

questions.question_text: The phrase 'shall identify the current temperature value as an invalid temperature and shall output an invalid temperature status' combines two separate actions. Should this requirement be split into two distinct requirements—one for identifying the current temperature value as invalid, and another for outputting the invalid temperature status?

answers.answer_text: Keep this as one requirement. The bundled actions describe a single causal step (one trigger producing one behavior), not two independently testable behaviors -- splitting would fragment one atomic step rather than separate genuinely distinct requirements.

test_strategy.rationale: Equivalence partitioning applies because temperature inputs are divided into valid and invalid numeric ranges. Boundary value analysis applies because specific numeric thresholds ('strictly less than the lower value' and 'strictly greater than the upper value') define critical boundaries between valid and invalid inputs. Decision table applies because multiple combined conditions (temperature below lower bound vs. above upper bound) drive the invalid output status.

test_cases.title: Equivalence Partitioning - Input temperature well below valid range lower bound
test_cases.preconditions: THEMAS system is configured with valid temperature range [0.0°C, 100.0°C].
steps: Input a temperature value of -25.0°C, which belongs to the invalid partition strictly less than the lower bound (0.0°C).
Observe system identification and output status.
test_cases.expected_result: The THEMAS system identifies -25.0°C as an invalid temperature and outputs an invalid temperature status.

test_cases.title: Equivalence Partitioning - Input temperature well above valid range upper bound
test_cases.preconditions: THEMAS system is configured with valid temperature range [0.0°C, 100.0°C].
steps: Input a temperature value of 150.0°C, which belongs to the invalid partition strictly greater than the upper bound (100.0°C).
Observe system identification and output status.
test_cases.expected_result: The THEMAS system identifies 150.0°C as an invalid temperature and outputs an invalid temperature status.

test_cases.title: Boundary Value Analysis - Temperature value immediately below lower bound
test_cases.preconditions: THEMAS system lower bound of valid temperature range is set to 0.0°C.
steps: Provide a temperature reading of -0.1°C, immediately across the lower boundary (strictly less than lower bound).
test_cases.expected_result: The system identifies -0.1°C as an invalid temperature and outputs an invalid temperature status.

test_cases.title: Boundary Value Analysis - Temperature value immediately above upper bound
test_cases.preconditions: THEMAS system upper bound of valid temperature range is set to 100.0°C.
steps: Provide a temperature reading of 100.1°C, immediately across the upper boundary (strictly greater than upper bound).
test_cases.expected_result: The system identifies 100.1°C as an invalid temperature and outputs an invalid temperature status.

test_cases.title: Decision Table - Condition Temp < Lower Bound is True
test_cases.preconditions: Valid temperature range is defined as [0.0°C, 100.0°C].
steps: Evaluate decision table rule: Condition 1 (Temp < 0.0°C) = TRUE, Condition 2 (Temp > 100.0°C) = FALSE.
Send temperature input to THEMAS system.
test_cases.expected_result: System triggers the decision rule outcome: identifies the temperature as invalid and outputs an invalid temperature status.

test_cases.title: Decision Table - Condition Temp > Upper Bound is True
test_cases.preconditions: Valid temperature range is defined as [0.0°C, 100.0°C].
steps: Evaluate decision table rule: Condition 1 (Temp < 0.0°C) = FALSE, Condition 2 (Temp > 100.0°C) = TRUE.
Send temperature input to THEMAS system.
test_cases.expected_result: System triggers the decision rule outcome: identifies the temperature as invalid and outputs an invalid temperature status.
